sideways/recall: Batch norm normalizes each feature over the examples in a batch: down a column.
sideways/rows: Layer norm turns that sideways. It normalizes each example over its own features: along a row.
sideways/alone: So an example's output depends on that example alone. The batch size does not matter, and training and test work the same way, with no running averages.
one/x: Take one example with four features: nine, three, seventeen and eleven.
one/var: The squared distances from it, one, forty nine, forty nine and one, average to twenty five, so the standard deviation is five.
one/xhat: Subtract the mean and divide by the standard deviation: nine becomes minus zero point two, three becomes minus one point four. Epsilon only guards against dividing by zero.
one/gamma: Then, as in batch norm, a learned scale, gamma, and shift, beta, with one entry of each per feature. With d features, that is two d learned numbers.
